topIssues.title: Kona and op-node can disagree on brotli channels
topIssues.author: kevin-valerio
topIssues.body:
## Bugs description
This issue actually contains two distinct bugs that can cause divergence between Kona and op-node for brotli-compressed channels.

- Bug 1: `decompress_brotli` can return `Ok()` even when brotli decompression did **not** reach `ResultSuccess`.
- Bug 2: Kona selects brotli based on the leading version byte and only later gates Fjord using `batch.timestamp`. op-node gates brotli **up front** using the L1 inclusion context (`isFjord`).

If a system uses Kona in a fault proof program / dispute game, these divergences can lead to incorrect outputs becoming accepted on Kona, while being refused on op-node. 

### `decompress_brotli` returns `Ok()` without requiring `ResultSuccess`

`decompress_brotli` loops only while the decoder returns `NeedsMoreOutput`. If the decoder returns `NeedsMoreInput` or `ResultFailure`, the loop stops and the function still returns `Ok(output_truncated_to_written_bytes)`.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/brotli.rs#L44-L73

Kona can treat invalid or truncated brotli as "valid decompressed bytes" (even if potentially empty), returning `Ok(vec![])` or `Ok(partial_bytes)`. The function only errors when the output would exceed `max_rlp_bytes_per_channel` (`BatchTooLarge`).

This is a divergence against op-node behavior that streams decompression through `brotli.NewReader(...)` and propagate errors during RLP decode if the brotli stream is truncated or invalid.

###  Fjord brotli gating is checked too late and uses a different time basis
In Kona, `BatchReader::decompress` decides "this is brotli" from the first byte (`CHANNEL_VERSION_BROTLI == 1`) and then decompresses the rest. `BatchReader::next_batch` only rejects brotli *after* decoding a batch, by checking Fjord using `cfg.is_fjord_active(batch.timestamp())`.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/reader.rs#L95-L98


https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/reader.rs#L117-L120

However, in op-node, brotli is gated **up front** using the L1 inclusion context (`isFjord`). If it’s not Fjord, op-node rejects brotli immediately.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/op-node/rollup/derive/channel.go#L193-L197

Kona and op-node can disagree on whether brotli is acceptable around Fjord, because Kona’s check is based on **`batch.timestamp()` (L2 data)** and happens **after** decompression+decode, while op-node’s check is based on the **L1 inclusion context** and happens **before** setting up the brotli reader.
 
### Risk for the truncated brotli stream being accepted by Kona (bug 1)
A buggy authorized batch submitter sends an L1 batch inbox transaction whose channel starts with the brotli version byte `0x01`. An actor crafts a brotli stream that starts decompressing into a valid RLP-encoded batch, then truncates the brotli data so the decoder ends in `NeedsMoreInput` (not `ResultSuccess`). `op-node` brotli is streamed via `brotli.NewReader`, and the RLP decode fails due to invalid decompression. Kona `decompress_brotli` returns `Ok(partial_bytes)` and the batch decode can succeed from those bytes. Kona derives a different output than op-node. 

### Risk for pre-Fjord inclusion but post-Fjord batch timestamp (bug 2)
Assume `fjord_time = 2_000`. An actor submits a brotli channel (first byte `0x01`) in an L1 inclusion context with `origin.timestamp = 1_999` (pre-Fjord). The decoded batch inside the channel uses `batch.timestamp = 2_000` (Fjord-active by timestamp). `op-node`'s `isFjord == false` based on L1 inclusion context, so brotli is rejected immediately. 

However brotli decompression runs, the batch is decoded, and the Fjord check uses `cfg.is_fjord_active(batch.timestamp()) == true`, so the batch can be accepted. Kona accepts brotli data that op-node rejects, again creating derivation divergence risk.

### Fix for the first bug
Change `decompress_brotli` to return an error unless `BrotliDecompressStream()` reaches `BrotliResult::ResultSuccess`. Handle `NeedsMoreInput` and `ResultFailure` as errors, not as "success with partial output".

### Fix for the second bug
Gate brotli before decompression using the L1 inclusion context, as op-node’s `isFjord` is doing. Pass an `is_fjord`/`origin_timestamp` decision into the Kona `BatchReader` and reject brotli channels pre-Fjord.

## Author notes
This bug was initially reported in Immunefi but closed since considered as out-of-scope. These bugs were found using a differential fuzzing approach and [gosentry](https://github.com/kevin-valerio/gosentry).

topIssues.title: interop + batcher: Use Verification-Aware CurrentL1
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
The Batcher watches "CurrentL1" for the chain it is publishing, and does not expect this value to go backwards. However, if it is making calls into the Virtual Node, it is actually fetching the "Local" CurrentL1 view, which may revert on block invalidation/replacement.

The batcher should have a way to get a non-reverting view of currentL1 for this progression check. Currently the SuperRoot API does this by computing the minimum verified in addition to the local progression.

Batcher should fetch similar data in order to avoid getting stuck during reorgs, as is currently experienced in interop dev networks.

**Claude:** Reporting flaky test encountered in CI.

## Test
`TestWithdrawal_Permissioned` in `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-acceptance-tests/tests/base/withdrawal/permissioned`

## CI Runs
- **memory-all-opn-op-geth:** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/123586/workflows/3ab343a1-567f-44d3-a0e1-78b86d3b675b/jobs/4913300
  - Branch: merge-queue commit \`af44e3fa\` for #20343
  - Test ran 50.37s before failing

## Date
2026-04-24

## Failure
```
=== RUN   TestWithdrawal_Permissioned
    assertions.go:387:
        Error Trace:    op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go:191
                        op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go:181
                        op-devstack/dsl/bridge.go:182
                        op-acceptance-tests/tests/base/withdrawal/withdrawal_test_helper.go:63
        Error:          Received unexpected error:
                        upstream dep 0 (*plan.Lazy[*github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/core/types.Receipt]) failed:
                        upstream dep 1 (*plan.Lazy[struct {}]) failed:
                        operation failed permanently after 5 attempts: nonce too low: next nonce 1, tx nonce 0
        Test:           TestWithdrawal_Permissioned
        Messages:       must transact
--- FAIL: TestWithdrawal_Permissioned (50.37s)
```

## Notes
- Failure looks like a nonce race in the EOA/transaction-management path (`op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go:191`). Two transactions sharing an account, the second submitted with stale nonce 0 while the first already advanced the chain to nonce 1.
- Encountered while merging an unrelated PR (#20343) which only touches `op-devstack/presets/singlechain_from_runtime.go` and `op-devstack/sysgo/{l2_cl_opnode,singlechain_build}.go` — none of those should affect withdrawal nonces.

A fix branch will follow.

topPRs.author: jyellick
topPRs.body:
## Summary

The `ghcr.io/paradigmxyz/op-reth` image our compose files reference is no longer maintained — op-reth ownership moved to OP Labs at v1.11.0. The new authoritative image at `us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth` does **not** include Boba as a built-in chain (the superchain-registry compile-time integration was dropped during the move).

This PR switches to the OP Labs image and supplies the Boba chain spec at runtime via a mounted JSON file.

- Add `boba-community/chainspecs/{boba,boba-sepolia}.json` (1.5KB each) extracted from `paradigmxyz/op-reth:v1.10.2 dump-genesis`
- Add `chainspecs/README.md` documenting the why and a regeneration procedure
- Switch `RETH_IMAGE` default to `us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth`, pin `RETH_VERSION` to `v2.2.1`
- Mount the chain spec JSON in compose files; replace `--chain=boba[-sepolia]` with `--chain=/config/<chain>.json`
- Update geth-to-reth migration guide and boba-docs to reflect the new image and mount

## Validation

Tested against a live Boba Sepolia snapshot using the new image + JSON chain spec:
- The OP Labs `op-reth:v2.2.1` opens the existing v1.10.2-format database without migration
- Sync resumes from the snapshot block and advances forward
- `op-node:v1.16.5` drives op-reth correctly via the Engine API
- `eth_chainId` returns `0x70d2` (28882) as expected

The extracted chain spec produces a byte-identical `OpChainSpec` when reloaded by the new image:
```bash
docker run --rm ghcr.io/paradigmxyz/op-reth:v1.10.2 dump-genesis --chain boba | tail -n +2 > /tmp/a.json
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/boba-community/chainspecs:/cs" us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-reth:v2.2.1 \
  dump-genesis --chain /cs/boba.json | tail -n +2 > /tmp/b.json
diff /tmp/a.json /tmp/b.json  # no diff
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Pull this branch and run `docker compose -f docker-compose-boba-sepolia-reth.yml up -d` against an existing reth-data directory; verify sync continues from current head
- [ ] Verify `eth_chainId` returns 28882 (sepolia) / 288 (mainnet)
- [ ] (optional) Run the migration `init` profile against a fresh state dump and confirm `init-state` produces an identical state root with the new `--chain=/config/<chain>.json` argument
